reviewedBy: OpenAI Codex technical dependency review (AI; maintainer-delegated public maintenance; not legal advice)

rationale: The upstream v1.58.0 CHANGELOG.md adopts SQLite 3.53.4 and its journal-rollback fix, replacing the local recovery patch retained in v1.57.0. Its go.mod requires libc v1.75.6 and memory v1.12.1; these are upgraded together rather than mixing generated SQLite code with another libc ABI.

The exact sqlite BSD and public-domain license texts, libc BSD and complete third-party notices, and memory BSD-3-Clause, Go and mmap-go texts are byte-identical to the prior artifact profile. Their new source module versions and verified checksums are recorded without weakening byte-hash verification.

The 2026-09-18 maintenance migrates the exact Go toolchain from 1.26.8 to 1.27.1 together with go.mod, Docker version guards, CI and license inventories. The Docker Official Image index 648f440f42a0958804efb24df176f806f9d353b41f1c0627f666428e40310f6b contains linux/amd64 manifest 6860a573025fcd35aba4f1b23e858b1c1dcd425d53fa73562e169a6ab1c2339a. The Go LICENSE and PATENTS bytes remain unchanged. The x/image, x/sys and x/text modules are updated together to v0.46.0, v0.48.0 and v0.42.0; SQLite and its libc/memory versions are unchanged.

The optional sqlite/vec package remains excluded: neither entrypoint imports it and both unstripped Linux binaries have zero matching vec symbols. memory v1.12.1 also carries a README logo and LICENSE-LOGO locator (SHA-256 5ae5bee3072a841376451b48d8cfcec7188e10543926d5870828d36c8a750dc5); no memory Go file embeds the logo, and neither that image nor the module source/cache is copied into the runtime.

The project still uses the default sqlite driver, sql.Open, and its existing WAL/busy-timeout PRAGMA DSNs. No OFD environment variable, OFDLocking call, new source query, schema migration, or runtime component is introduced by this maintenance update.
residualRisks: SQLite v1.58.0 exposes opt-in Linux OFD locking, off by default upstream. This change does not enable it; enabling it later changes process-wide database-file locking while WAL shared-memory coordination remains POSIX and requires a separate compatibility review.

Importing sqlite/vec or distributing memory's README logo or module sources in a later artifact changes the reviewed boundary and requires the corresponding notices and a new inventory review before release.

Go 1.27 changes the runtime, compiler and standard-library implementations. Passing native tests, Linux cross-build/linkage checks and synthetic reader tests does not exclude all regressions; the exact Linux container still requires its independent release gates before publication.

Passing module verification, native Go tests and vet, the reachable-vulnerability scan, and Linux cross-build/linkage inspection reduces but does not eliminate regression risk. This is a delegated AI technical artifact review, not an independent legal opinion or final publication authorization.
